newTerms.Trust and Spiritual Preparedness (sermon: La confianza y la preparación espiritual

forcedChoices.choice: ustedes for Jesus' address to the crowd
forcedChoices.reason: Plural address; the Spanish rules require ustedes.

forcedChoices.choice: tú when the young man speaks to Jesus, and when Andrew (165:5.1), the other man (165:4.5), and Peter (165:6.1) speak to him
forcedChoices.reason: Disciples and listeners address a teacher, not a ruler or judge; tú matches the close address of the scenes.
"over you" covers the two brothers; "Where did you get" speaks to the young man only.
The sense is possession; the earlier glossary gives "demonios" for possession, not "diablo".
Lowercase master of servants; «Maestro» would read as Jesus' title.

forcedChoices.choice: «no su sirviente, sino su amo» (masculine) for wealth
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces a gender; the masculine nouns keep the servant/master contrast general.

forcedChoices.choice: «no puedo hacerlo» for "I may not do"
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish poder keeps both readings open: lack of ability and lack of permission.
